amendments.reason: Applied audit patches 1, 2a, 2b, 2c, 3 and 4a from docs/INSTRUCTION-AUDIT.md. The set specified the product well and contracted it poorly: no scope limit in the always-loaded file, no phase exit criteria, and no requirement to enumerate trusted values before coding, which permitted a working answer-disclosure exploit. These patches add the active-scope rule, the instruction priority order, mandatory module pairs, per-phase exit criteria, the implementation-state vocabulary and completeness sweep, the completion report with forbidden claims, the section 41.1 trust-boundary review, and server-authoritative policy inputs in section 29.

Registered docs/progress.md as the standing twelve-phase progress ledger and a mandatory per-session deliverable. The instruction set required a plan, assumptions and a log, but nothing tracked cumulative completion against phase exit criteria, so completion state was only discoverable by a fresh audit. Section 57.5 also records why the ledger and SPEC-AUDIT.md measure different things.

scoring-v1 was audited by execution and found to reward disengagement: skipping the transfer task scored 100 while attempting it for partial credit scored 79. Section 13 also left the difficulty adjustment and reasoning rubric unspecified. Section 57 adds the session-log requirement that the original instruction set lacked.
